name: Saint Bartholomew the Apostle
history: One of the Twelve, generally identified with Nathanael of Cana, whom Philip brought to Jesus. Christ greeted him as an Israelite in whom there is no guile. Tradition holds that he carried the Gospel as far as India and Armenia, and that he was martyred by being flayed alive.
life: Bartholomew appears in each list of the apostles beside Philip, and since early times he has been identified with Nathanael in the Gospel of John. When Philip told him they had found the Messiah, Jesus of Nazareth, Nathanael replied, Can anything good come out of Nazareth? Philip simply said, Come and see. Jesus told him He had seen him under the fig tree before Philip called him, and Nathanael answered, Rabbi, you are the Son of God. Later he was among the disciples to whom the risen Christ appeared by the Sea of Tiberias. Eusebius records a tradition that he took the Gospel of Matthew to India. Armenian tradition says he was martyred in Armenia, flayed and beheaded. Artists show him holding a knife, and in Michelangelo’s Last Judgment he holds his own skin. His relics are honoured in Rome on the island in the Tiber.
prayerTo: Saint Bartholomew, you came and saw, and confessed Jesus as the Son of God. Pray that I may be without guile, honest with God and with others. When I doubt, bring me back to Christ, and give me courage to bear witness to Him whatever it costs. Amen.
penance: Be scrupulously honest today in small things, and ask a friend who is searching to come and see, perhaps to Mass or a talk.
meditation: Come and see. Philip did not argue with his friend; he brought him to Jesus. Whom could you invite to come and see?
prayer: Almighty, eternal God, Who bestowed on us the devout and holy joy of this day to celebrate the feast of Your blessed Apostle Bartholomew, grant unto Your Church, we beseech You, both to love what he believed and to preach what he taught. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
